scope: Proposition 6.4 (Bounded correspondences cannot sweep the bundle) of the manuscript “Fourfold nonvanishing by minimal metrics and moving jets” (preprints/Fourfold-nonvanishing-by-minimal-metrics-and-moving-jets-September-27-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 034 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 1946d50201ab1ae0), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 23. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix ϵ > 0, an integer q > 0, and positive constants B0, B1. Keep Y, K, A, Lt and P = L1 +L2 +qξ as above. For all sufficiently small positive rational t, there is no irreducible finite-type parameter space T and integral closed subvariety Γ ⊂ T × Z, dominant over T, with the following properties: (i) The evaluation Γ → Z is dominant, and a general fiber V over T is an integral subvariety of dimension n. (ii) On a smooth projective resolution V ∗ → V , both projections gi : V ∗ → Y , i = 1, 2, are dominant and generically finite. (iii) Writing P also for its pullback to V ∗, one has 0 < Pn · V ≤ B0, KV ∗ Pn−1 ≤ B1(Pn · V ). The restriction on t depends only on the fixed geometry and ϵ, q, B0, B1, not on the parameter space or family.
